title: 约翰霍普金斯专家：每个麻疹病例4.3万美元，这笔钱本可省下，为何还要花？
speaker: Dr. Amish Adolgez

segments.en: So anytime there's an infectious disease, it will lead to disruption. People can't go about their activities of daily life.
segments.zh: 任何传染病都会导致混乱，人们无法正常进行日常活动。

segments.en: Which means if it's a child of measles, that child can't go to school, that child's parents might have to stay home, that child's parents might have to hire someone to babysit.
segments.zh: 如果孩子患麻疹，不能上学，父母可能得请假或雇人照看。

segments.en: And then you have a health department that then has to go and investigate who was the person in touch with? Do they need to contact people?
segments.zh: 卫生部门还需调查接触者，进行追踪。

segments.en: Do they need to do any kind of countermeasures to stop the measles from spreading in a given community? All of that costs money.
segments.zh: 是否需要采取措施阻止传播？所有这些都需要花钱。

segments.en: And it's money that doesn't need to be spent because these measles cases are happening voluntarily by people's choices.
segments.zh: 这些本不必花费，因为麻疹病例是人为选择的结果。

segments.en: This is not some force of nature. This is people's choice to not vaccinate their children. And then it has economic consequences that don't need to be incurred.
segments.zh: 这不是自然力量，而是人们选择不给孩子接种疫苗，导致了本可避免的经济后果。

segments.en: And I think that's another important point to make with infectious diseases is that they keep humans from flourishing.
segments.zh: 传染病阻碍人类发展，这是另一个重要观点。

segments.en: Because they're stuck in bed sick and they're not out there producing, they're out there innovating, and you're taking money that could be used for some other concern.
segments.zh: 人们因病卧床，无法生产创新，资金被挪用到本不该花的地方。

segments.en: Now it's being put back to something, it's putting into something that we shouldn't have to be putting money into when we've had a solution to this since the 1960s.
segments.zh: 这些钱被投入到本不必投入的地方，而解决方案自1960年代就已存在。
